candidates.buyer: Individual owners and micro-hosts renting 1-7 rooms or flats on Airbnb/Booking (CNP holders, no company), plus small guesthouse owners. The number of hosts is not given in the sources.

candidates.existing: Competitor searches (e-Factura/host software, SITUR code assistance) found no dedicated product. Only free SPV e-Factura app, general accountants and the platforms' own tax pages. The code itself is issued by the state (SITUR).
candidates.name: Short-term rental host compliance kit: unique registration code, listing sync, VAT/e-Factura/D212 calendar
candidates.trigger: Regulation (EU) 2024/1028 applies from 20 May 2026: a unique code per unit via SITUR, shown in every listing, with platforms delisting listings without it. Tax: 30% forfait for 1-7 rooms, special VAT code with Form 301 and 390 by the 25th for platform commission invoices, annual D212 by 25 May. RO e-Factura for individual hosts from 1 Jun 2026 (Form 082) is disputed because Law 88/2026 may have made it optional.
candidates.unchecked: Whether SITUR code issuance now works (Oct 2026) and whether a national law was adopted. Status of Law 88/2026 on e-Factura. Number of hosts. Whether hosts will pay for a done-for-you service. Whether an API or bulk route exists for agents.

candidates.existing: No competitor search run (budget exhausted). Distribution companies (Engie, Axpo, Gazest) publish the procedure and general ERP or field-service tools probably exist (unverified).

candidates.trigger: ANRE Order 179/2015 (consolidated 14 Dec 2025): verification at most every 2 years, revision at most every 10 years, only by EDIB-authorised firms. Firms must keep a current register per consumption point. The operator can cut supply the day it finds a missing check. Draft: revision replaces that year's verification.
candidates.unchecked: Competitor search. Number of EDIB firms. Whether the distribution operators already run a free portal for results. Related to K02 (ISCIR workbench) but a different regulator and buyer; possible shared product.

candidates.trigger: Law 162/2026 and Joint Order 1229/598/2182/2026 (MO 789, 17 Sep 2026): monthly report within 20 days through e-guvernare.ro; Declaration 183. Period 7 Aug-31 Oct 2026, extendable.

coverage.category: 21. Fuel stations and fuel or LPG distributors
coverage.found: New temporary duty: Legea 162/2026 (MO 642, 4 Aug 2026) caps fuel markups at the 2025 average for the crisis period 7 Aug-31 Oct 2026 (extendable). Joint Order 1229/598/2182/2026 (MO 789, 17 Sep 2026) requires every petrol/diesel importer, producer, distributor and retailer, including small stations, to file a monthly markup report within 20 days via e-guvernare.ro using the authorities' assistance program. Declaration 183 (annual average markup 2025) was due within 5 days of its order. The tool is a state program and the rule is temporary, so the case is weak (see ledger). No LPG-specific ANRE/ANAF duty found. ANAF high-risk-firm pre-notification draft (1 Apr 2026) not confirmed adopted.

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: Monthly stock reporting to the MADR online platform (due by the 15th, for stocks at the end of the previous month) has applied since Nov 2023 to producers, storers, processors and traders of cereals, oilseeds, fruit and veg, meat and dairy. Shops up to 400 sqm of sales area, street traders and catering are exempt. Fine sources disagree. No ANSVSA grain-warehouse register found. No competitor tool found for the monthly stock report.

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: Casele de ajutor reciproc (CAR) are non-profit employee/pensioner loan associations under Law 122/1996 and GO 26/2000. They keep accounts under OMFP 1969/2007, with a live question whether they file SAF-T D406. Not under ASF. Agricultural co-operatives (Law 566/2004, as amended by Law 265/2020) must file annual financial statements or risk dissolution after 2 years' delay, and ONRC publishes lists of delinquents. A national agricultural co-operative register is run by MADR. Nothing new in 2026. Neither segment is clearly large.

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes
coverage.found: MS Order 1090/2026 (in force 8 May 2026) changes the rules for setting up and running medical cabinets and their entry in the Registrul unic al cabinetelor medicale: personnel lists, employment and collaboration contracts (a 30-day filing to DSP is mentioned, unconfirmed), suspension. CNAS SIUI reporting continues. CNAS postponed mandatory use of the electronic ID card for providers. A CNAS draft order limits private providers in national programmes. The segment is well served by clinic software, so it is weak.

coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals or precursors
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond existing duties. Serialisation checks via OSMR/SNVM have been in force since 2019. ANM enforcement tables (Oct 2025) list pharmacies fined for expired stock. Opioid pharmacies were checked in 2023. The controlled-substance list was extended in Oct 2024. No 2026 rule or register change found.

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: A 2026 emergency ordinance (reported May 2026, number and text not found) ends periodic licence renewal for security and alarm firms. It brings new rules on the physical-security risk assessment (done by an evaluator in the RNERSF register), simplified unarmed guarding and extra duties. ITM enforcement on security firms is heavy (a 600k lei fine in Bucharest). No 2026 change for temporary-work agencies found. The reform lowers the burden, so it is weak.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: The new CATUC code (urbanism and construction code) is reported in force from 25 Aug 2026 (one opinion article only). It brings certification of construction firms by experience and specialisation. Site managers (diriginți de șantier) gained fire-safety duties in a March 2026 ordinance. Site managers are authorised by ISC, and the technical book of the building is their duty (fine up to 10k lei). No e-Construcții duty for small firms confirmed.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: Under Law 129/2019, real-estate agents and developers must keep an ONPCSB online notification current (15 days, fine 5k-10k lei, platform on onpcsb.ro). ONPCSB has a real-estate suspicious-transaction guide. The beneficial-owner declaration to ONRC is due within 15 days of any change. Nothing new for 2026 found for notaries. ONPCSB's own free portal handles reporting.

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: Regulation (EU) 2024/1028 applies from 20 May 2026. Every short-term rental unit needs a unique registration code, issued through SITUR (login by ROeID or e-signature) and shown in the listing. In May 2026 code generation was not yet available. Platforms will delist listings with no valid code and report monthly data. The MEDAT minister also announced a digital guest slip. Tax: forfait of 30% of gross for 1-7 rooms, special VAT code with Form 301 and 390 for platform commissions, and ANAF found tens of thousands of undeclared hosts in one county. RO e-Factura for individual hosts by CNP from 1 Jun 2026 (Form 082 by 26 May) is contradicted by a source saying Law 88/2026 (MO 459, 29 May 2026) made it optional. Local tourist promotion taxes: Sibiu 2% from Jan 2026, Brașov 1 leu per tourist per day (draft). The 2011-13 SIET tourist register never launched.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: Budget used on other categories. Timber and EUDR is already K07 (rejected). Fish, honey, other food exporters and importer certification were not searched.

coverage.category: 31. Social services: private elderly-care homes and care centres (accreditation, licence, inspections)
coverage.found: Law 292/2011 requires accreditation, then an operating licence, recorded in the Registrul Electronic Unic al Serviciilor Sociale. In 2023 about 1,350 unaccredited operators were identified against 338 licensed homes. A tougher regime was announced (provisional licence cut from 12 to 3 months, unannounced inspections, criminal sanctions, fines up to 100k lei), final adoption unconfirmed. AJPIS Cluj ran 29 control campaigns Jan-Aug 2026 and fined an unlicensed home 80k lei (reported 2 Sep 2026).

coverage.category: 32. Authorised auto workshops and ITP stations (RAR)
coverage.found: Since 1 Dec 2024 RAR issues the RAR Auto-Pass certificate. Authorised workshops and ITP stations must send the VIN and odometer reading for every service, plus main repairs and odometer repairs, to RAR. A software vendor (WinMentor Enterprise, doc rev. 23 May 2025) already ships a module for it. Whether the certificate is mandatory for sellers is unclear in the sources.

coverage.category: 33. Beverage retailers under the SGR deposit-return system
coverage.found: HG 1074/2021: every retailer selling SGR-packaged drinks, large or small, must register in the RetuRO database, sign a contract, take back packaging, and keep sales records. It must report with the administrator's own software. Garda de Mediu fines are heavy (over 760k lei in one round, up to 50k lei per refusal to refund the deposit). RetuRO sent a letter to retailers on 8 May 2026 on the 2026 handling fee. The reporting tool is the administrator's, as in K09.

coverage.category: 34. Natural-gas installation inspection firms (ANRE EDIB/PDIB) and households and HOAs as consumers
coverage.found: ANRE Order 179/2015 (consolidated Dec 2025) requires technical verification at most every 2 years and technical revision at most every 10 years for gas installations, done only by ANRE-authorised EDIB firms. Authorised firms must keep a current register of verifications and revisions per contracted consumption point. The network operator can cut supply when the verification is missing. A draft would let the 10-year revision replace that year's verification (adoption unconfirmed). Appliances are separately checked by ISCIR-authorised operators.

The 2025-26 reforms (Law 141/2025 package) add ONJN binding orders. A public register of gaming devices with map and QR codes was announced for 15 Oct 2025. A March 2026 emergency ordinance reportedly requires a local operating authorisation in addition to the national licence. A self-exclusion unification draft is pending. ONJN ran about 7,000 checks in its first year, with fines near 8.1M lei. The sector is chain-dominated, so it is weak.

coverage.category: 36. Agricultural producers selling directly: producer attestation and sales booklet (Law 145/2014)
coverage.found: Individual producers need an atestat de producător (valid 1 year, visa by the mayor each half year) and a carnet de comercializare, with a sheet handed to each buyer. Mayors keep a register. This is a paper process, and fines reach 22,500 lei in older sources. No digital version found in 2026. Duty-holders are individuals and the registers belong to city halls.

OUG 17/2026 (in force Mar 2026) amends Law 307/2006. Authorisations can be suspended when detection, extinguishing or lighting systems do not work or documentation is missing, with about 30 days to fix. There is no warning for many firm offences, and reduced-fine payment is withdrawn for serious ones. IGSU must publish a live list of authorisations. A MAI draft would force medium firms to form fire-protection technical commissions (final form unconfirmed). No mandatory PSI register or periodic deadline for SMEs confirmed.
